Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a focal opacity in the right lung apex (indicated by the yellow arrow) with associated destruction/erosion of the adjacent first rib, which is the classic radiographic appearance of a Pancoast tumour (superior sulcus tumour). This diagnosis fits the patient's profile as an elderly long-term smoker and explains the neurological symptoms (disorientation) via potential metastatic disease or paraneoplastic syndromes, whereas the other options do not typically present with this specific apical mass and rib invasion pattern.
